artifacts.summary: Confirms cslib findings (a)/(b), recommends Option (ii) -- formally admit ## Plan Deviations as an optional summary-format.md section given 11/16 implementation agents already use it -- and corrects the task's premise that web/lean-base already conform (they do not); audits all extension implementation agents for the same failure mode.

memory_candidates.content: validate-artifact.sh's summary/report/plan checks only flag MISSING required sections/metadata fields (grep -qE "^##+ Section" / grep -qF "**Field**:"); it never rejects extra headings. Any implementation agent can safely add domain-specific sections (e.g. ## Plan Deviations, ## Verification) alongside the six required summary-format.md headings without tripping gate-out errors -- gate-out failures come from REPLACING required headings, not adding extra ones.

Several extension implementation agents follow a base/hard asymmetry where the -hard variant references summary-format.md but the base variant does not (observed in both cslib and lean extensions). When auditing one extension's base/hard pair for a context-reference gap, check sibling extensions' base/hard pairs for the same asymmetry rather than assuming it's isolated.

## Plan Deviations is a de facto ecosystem-wide summary section (used/mandated by 11 of 16 implementation-terminus agents: general, general-hard, cslib both, nvim, nix, web, latex, python, typst, z3, lean-base) despite not being documented in core summary-format.md. It captures the progress-file deviations array's skipped/altered/deferred taxonomy, a distinct concern from ## Decisions or ## Follow-ups.
